newsitem.title: USA: Conn. firms pay less for workers compensation - Gov.
newsitem.headline: Conn. firms pay less for workers compensation - Gov.

text.p: Connecticut Gov. John Rowland said productivity gains will cut the cost borne by employers for workers' compensation in the 1997 fiscal year by $11.4 million, the largest fall since the system started in 1913.

Saying this is the third year in a row that the program's operating costs have fallen, Rowland said on Wednesday in prepared remarks that firms will be assessed at a 1.21 percent rate, down from three percent in last fiscal year.
Their total assessment is projected at $6.7 million.

The sharp drop in the program's costs is expected make the state more competitive. "In Connecticut, we are driving down the costs of doing business here to help the private sector retain and create jobs," Rowland said.

Connecticut also is obtaining royalties from a vendor who designed the state's new computer system for the program and is selling it to other states. Each resale will provide $100,000 in royalties, and the first of two $50,000 installments from this source is being paid.
